about.descriptor: Engineer bridging the gap between academic ML and production RF reality.
about.bio_1: I specialize in deploying AI agent workflows that actually survive the transition from synthetic data to the messy reality of RF measurements. My focus is on building tools that turn complex signal data into actionable insights for non-technical engineers.
about.bio_2: At National Instruments, I built an end-to-end AI agent skill for NI Nigel, optimizing data pipelines with Polars and Parquet to handle large-scale manufacturing datasets. I've learned that the most valuable AI isn't the one with the highest SOTA score, but the one that provides a reliable root-cause analysis in production.
about.bio_3: Currently pursuing an M.Sc. in Electromobility at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, focusing on AI and Connectivity. I'm looking for roles where I can wrestle with actual deployments and build agentic workflows that solve real-world engineering bottlenecks.

ni_agent.name: Production AI Agent for RF Analytics
ni_agent.problem: Manufacturing engineers needed complex root-cause analysis across 40+ test types without manual coding
ni_agent.tech: Python · Polars · Parquet · LLM Agent Skill · Plotly
ni_agent.description: Designed and deployed an end-to-end Accept-on-Retest (AoR) analytics framework as a production skill for NI Nigel. I replaced pandas with Polars and implemented Parquet caching to drastically cut redundant data requests. The result was a natural-language interface that allowed engineers to query parametric test data and receive automated 1σ-3σ band classification summaries and visualizations.
ni_agent.what_went_wrong: Initially underestimated the overhead of repeatedly querying large-scale metadata. The system was stable but too slow for a conversational interface.
ni_agent.what_id_change: Move heavy data processing to the edge with a robust caching layer. Performance in an AI agent is as important as accuracy; if the agent takes 30 seconds to respond, the user stops using it.

mimo.name: MIMO Channel Estimation — The Real Data Problem
mimo.problem: Neural networks trained on synthetic channel data fail catastrophically in real deployments
mimo.description: Started with the textbook approach: generate perfect channel matrices, train CNN, achieve SOTA on paper. Then deployed to actual base station data and MSE went through the roof. The breakthrough? Augmenting synthetic data with measured channel impairments—multipath, noise, hardware nonlinearities. Phase 1 taught me that clean research data is the enemy of working ML systems.
mimo.what_went_wrong: Assumed academic datasets would translate to production reality. Spent 3 months trying to 'fix' the model when the data was broken all along.
mimo.what_id_change: Deploy to messy real data from day 1. The 'clean' training phase was a complete waste of time.

vlc.name: Vehicle-to-Vehicle Visible Light — When Physics Wins
vlc.problem: Low-latency V2V communication without RF spectrum allocation
vlc.description: VLC promises gigabit speeds, but nobody talks about what happens when it's cloudy. Built a prototype that worked perfectly indoors—10cm range, 100Mbps. Then tested outdoors and ambient light killed everything. Final solution: adaptive thresholding that detects daylight and switches to backup IR. The lesson: physics constraints always trump algorithmic cleverness.
vlc.what_went_wrong: Optimized for lab conditions first, then had to redesign everything for real-world lighting. Should have tested in daylight from day 1.
vlc.what_id_change: Start with the worst-case environment, not the best case. Physics doesn't care about your clean room results.
